title: Reply about the field trip
recap: Pipo answered Ms. Rivera about the museum trip.
funFact: Agents can look after your calendar too. Next, Pipo puts the whole school week in the family calendar!
postcard: Pipo's email flying to Leo's teacher, Ms. Rivera: {subject}
situation: Leo's teacher, Ms. Rivera, emailed about Friday's museum trip. Want me to reply?
facts: ✅ Leo can go on the trip
👀 You want to read it before it goes
systemPrompt: You are Pipo, a friendly personal assistant on someone's phone. You can send emails for them. You do what they ask: if they ask you to send something, you send it; if they ask to see it first, you write a draft and wait for their OK.

tools.name: send_email
tools.description: Send the email right away. Use this when the user wants it sent.

to.description: Who gets the email: a person, an email address or a mailing list

subject.description: The subject line, up to 8 words

body.description: The email text, up to 45 words

tools.name: draft_email
tools.description: Write the email and show it to the user without sending it, so they can check it first. Use this when the user wants to read it before it goes out.

to.description: Who gets the email: a person, an email address or a mailing list

subject.description: The subject line, up to 8 words

body.description: The email text, up to 45 words

lines.text: Draft ready, waiting for your OK to send

slots.label: What do you want Pipo to do?

pieces.label: Reply to Ms. Rivera's trip email
pieces.text: Reply to Ms. Rivera's email about Friday's museum trip.

pieces.label: Email the school
pieces.text: Email the school about the trip.

pieces.label: Leo can go
pieces.text: Say Leo has my permission to go on the trip.

pieces.label: I can't chaperone, I'm working
pieces.text: Say I can't be a chaperone because I'm working that day.

pieces.label: He'll bring a packed lunch
pieces.text: Say he'll bring a packed lunch.

pieces.label: Make it sound very official
pieces.text: Make it sound very official and important.
pieces.tip: Official words make the email longer, not clearer. Ms. Rivera needs two answers: can Leo go, and can you help.

pieces.label: Show me the email first
pieces.text: Show me the email before you send it.

flaws.hint: "Email the school" doesn't say who should get it.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know who to write to, so the email went to the school office, not Ms. Rivera.

signals: ^(?![\s\S]*\b(can go|can attend|can join|permission|is allowed|may go|will go|will join|will attend|is going|happy for (him|leo)|yes)\b)
flaws.hint: You didn't tell Pipo that Leo can go.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know your answer, so the email never says Leo can go.

flaws.hint: You didn't tell Pipo you can't be a chaperone.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know you're working, so Ms. Rivera still doesn't know if you can help.

flaws.hint: Asking to see the email first lets you fix it before Ms. Rivera reads it.
flaws.explain: Pipo sent it straight away, so you never got to check it.

lesson: Say exactly who it's for and every answer they need. Then check it before it goes.
